role: Statically scans this repo's RLS-table store modules for functions accepting tenantId as a bare, unverified parameter, and honestly stubs the live cross-tenant RLS read test that would require a real Postgres connection.
behaviorDescription: scanForUnverifiedTenantId() reads every .ts file in a given lib directory and flags exported functions accepting a bare `tenantId: string` parameter with no internal verification against a trusted auth source. Confirmed all 10 functions across purge-store.ts, incident-store.ts, and restraint-store.ts fit this pattern — the same class of gap already found and fixed elsewhere in this repo (89 files trusting a raw client header instead of JWT-verified context). Not yet exploitable, since nothing currently calls these functions from a live untrusted route, but a real contract obligation for whatever eventually does. attemptCrossTenantRead() is an honest stub: proving RLS enforcement itself holds requires a live Postgres connection this sandbox doesn't have.
hardStops: Never modifies any file on disk — strictly read-only static analysis
Never claims RLS enforcement itself is broken — the finding is specifically about the caller-responsibility gap in how tenantId reaches these functions
Never claims to have tested real cross-tenant reads — attemptCrossTenantRead() throws until a live Postgres connection is available to verify against
